video.title: Best AI Tool to Build Local Websites & Sell Them

summary: The host compares five AI website builders using the same prompts for a local business website, a website audit web app, and a lead generation landing page, then compares their pricing. The video presents AI-built websites and web apps as freelance services, with a basic site framed as a lower-priced offer and a complete client tool as a higher-priced one. Base44 ranks highest in the host’s tests, while Lovable is described as a strong option for marketing sites and landing pages. The comparison emphasizes working features, build time, correction effort, and predictable costs alongside visual quality.

speakers.name: Host
speakers.description: The host of the Mikey No Code channel; no personal name is stated in the transcript.

ideas.name: AI-built websites for local businesses
ideas.one_liner: Freelance building of professional websites for local businesses, using AI website builders.
ideas.customer: Local business owners, with examples including car washes, salons, cleaning companies, dentists, and contractors.
ideas.problem: They need a professional site that explains their service and makes it easy for customers to book or get in touch.
ideas.offer: Build a local business website with a hero, service packages, about section, testimonials, contact details, and a booking form.

price_points.label: a few hundred; currency not stated

pricing.notes: The host contrasts a site costing a few hundred with a more complete client tool costing at least 1,500 or more. No exact website price or currency is stated.

ideas.delivery: The freelancer uses an AI website builder to generate a site from a client-style prompt, then delivers the website. The host tested fictional car wash Sparkle Wash; no actual client delivery process is described.
unit_economics_claims: The host says a basic website may be charged at a few hundred, but does not state a currency or exact amount.
The host argues that time spent correcting layout problems cuts into freelance profit.

acquisition.how: No customer acquisition channel is described. Inbound enquiries could be handled with software, but winning bespoke local business projects is likely to need human sales and approval.

onboarding.how: A form could collect business details and site requirements; a person would likely review the brief before generation.

delivery.how: AI builders can generate much of the site, but a freelancer should check the content, functionality, and client-specific fit.

billing.how: Invoices and payment reminders could be automated with standard billing software; custom quotes may need human approval.

support.how: Routine questions could be answered with an agent, but site changes and business-specific requests need human review.

uk_applicability.notes: Local businesses need websites in the UK too. The transcript does not identify a US-only dependency.

risks: The host says correction time can turn a short client job into a much longer one, reducing profit.
Generated designs may look generic or fail to follow the client brief.
A UK provider handling contact or booking forms should account for privacy and consent requirements.

quotes.text: Almost every local business needs the same basic thing. A site that looks professional, that explains the service clearly, and that makes it easy for someone to book or to get in touch.
quotes.speaker: Host

quotes.text: The first build is a basic local business website because this is usually the easiest service for a freelancer to sell and also the one most clients ask for first.
quotes.speaker: Host

ideas.name: AI-powered client web apps
ideas.one_liner: Freelance building of more functional client tools with accounts, stored data, and AI features.

ideas.problem: A simple website may not provide the accounts, data storage, or working features a client needs.
ideas.offer: Build a client web app. The host’s example is a website audit tool that accepts a URL and returns SEO, performance, and usability scores with findings, authentication, and audit history.

price_points.label: at least 1,500 or more; currency not stated

pricing.notes: The host gives a broad comparison with basic sites costing a few hundred, but does not state a currency.

ideas.delivery: The freelancer builds an app with user accounts, data, and functionality using an AI builder. The host tested an audit app with URL input, AI-generated findings, scores, and user audit history; actual customer delivery is not described.
unit_economics_claims: The host says a complete client tool could be charged at least 1,500 or more, without stating a currency.
The host says longer build times and correction prompts can create deadline and margin risk.

acquisition.how: No acquisition channel is described. Inbound enquiries can be handled with software, but bespoke client sales and scoping are likely to need human input.

onboarding.how: A structured intake form could collect the brief and required features; a person should confirm scope and data needs.

delivery.how: AI can generate an initial app, but the host’s tests show errors, external API setup, and correction prompts can be necessary. Human end-to-end checks remain important.

billing.how: Billing and reminders could be automated, while a person approves project scope and any usage-based costs.

support.how: An agent could answer routine questions, but app bugs, account issues, and client-specific changes need human review.

uk_applicability.notes: Custom web apps can be built and sold to UK businesses. The transcript gives no US-only platform or legal dependency.

risks: A polished interface can conceal fake or non-working functionality.
Some builders require external API keys or additional services, adding setup and cost.
Build errors and correction prompts can make delivery times unpredictable.
A UK app that stores user accounts or audit history needs appropriate data handling.

ideas.name: Lead generation landing pages
ideas.one_liner: Freelance building of focused landing pages designed to collect leads or prompt sign-ups and bookings.
ideas.business_model: Freelance project fee; the host does not state a separate price for this service.
ideas.customer: Local businesses seeking enquiries, bookings, or email sign-ups; the host also demonstrates a fictional consumer app landing page.
ideas.problem: A regular website may not focus visitors on one clear action, such as signing up, booking, requesting a quote, or leaving an email.
ideas.offer: Build a focused landing page with a clear hero and call to action, feature and how-it-works sections, testimonials, and a lead capture form.

pricing.notes: The host says landing pages can be valuable but does not give a price for this service.

ideas.delivery: The freelancer generates a landing page using an AI builder, with content and layout leading visitors toward a form. The host’s test used a fictional wheel-of-names app called Spinpick.
unit_economics_claims: The host says a landing page can be more valuable than a regular website, but gives no price or revenue figures.

acquisition.how: The video does not say how clients are found. Inbound channels could be automated, but no specific channel or process is described.

onboarding.how: A form could collect the client’s offer, target audience, and call to action; a person should approve the brief.

delivery.how: An AI builder can generate the page and form, but a person should check the message, form behavior, and design.

billing.how: Invoices and reminders could be automated; the transcript does not discuss a billing process.

support.how: Routine questions could be handled by an agent, but edits to copy, forms, or integrations may need human review.

uk_applicability.notes: Landing pages and lead capture are applicable to UK businesses. A UK operator should ensure forms and follow-up marketing meet applicable privacy and consent rules.

risks: A page can include all requested sections but still feel generic or fail to guide visitors toward the form.
Lead capture requires reliable form behavior and appropriate handling of personal data.

quotes.text: For local businesses, a landing page can be more valuable than a regular website because it has one clear goal. It's built to get someone to sign up to book, request a quote, or leave their email.

tactics.name: Compare builders with identical client-style prompts
steps: Give each platform the same brief and requirements.
Test a local business website, a functional web app, and a lead generation landing page.
Record build time, errors, functionality, design quality, and correction prompts.
Judge whether the output is usable for a client, not just whether it looks finished.

quote.text: And we're not just judging on looks, build speed, errors, working functionality, native AI, authentication, publishing, pricing, and all the hidden costs nobody mentions until the invoice is due.
quote.speaker: Host

tactics.name: Use a structured brief for local business sites
steps: Specify the business and the desired visual style.
List the required hero, services, about, testimonials, contact information, and booking form.
Check that the generated site includes each requested section and is presentable to a client.

quote.text: include a hero section with a bold headline and a book now call to action, a services section showing three wash packages with pricing, an about section, a testimonial section with three customer reviews, and a contact section with location, hours, and a booking form.
quote.speaker: Host

tactics.name: Test apps end to end before delivery
steps: Test the primary feature with a real input.
Check that the report corresponds to that input rather than placeholder or fake output.
Verify authentication and saved history.
Include the time and effort required for corrections in the delivery plan.

quote.text: A static website can look good even if nothing is happening behind the scenes. A web app has to actually work.
quote.speaker: Host

tactics.name: Build landing pages toward one conversion action
steps: Use the hero to state the value and present a clear call to action.
Explain the features and how the product works.
Add testimonials to establish trust.
Make the lead capture form the natural next step.

quote.text: A good landing page should build momentum from the hero down, explain the value quickly, show how the product works, add some trust, and then make the email capture form feel like the natural next step.
quote.speaker: Host

tactics.name: Compare the full cost of delivering client projects
steps: Compare subscription prices and included credits.
Check whether AI, hosting, publishing, authentication, and database features are included.
Identify external API keys and services that add costs beyond the builder subscription.
Consider whether usage-based billing makes project costs hard to predict.

quote.text: Hosting and publishing and authentication, database access, AI features, credit limits, and hidden costs all matter here
quote.speaker: Host

tactics.name: Choose a builder based on the work being sold
steps: For front-end projects, check whether the builder produces fast, reliable websites and landing pages.
For client apps, test native AI and other core features without assuming a visual demo works.
Compare correction effort and recurring costs before choosing a platform for regular client work.

quote.text: If your offer is just front-end work, fine. Bolt can work for you. If you want to sell smarter web apps, it hits limits pretty quickly.
quote.speaker: Host
